name: Bigger Stacks
description: Raise the stack size of every stackable item in the world database.

sql.statement: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS yulon_stackable_backup (entry INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, stackable SMALLINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL) ENGINE=InnoDB;
sql.note: the undo, taken before anything is changed

sql.statement: INSERT IGNORE INTO yulon_stackable_backup (entry, stackable) SELECT entry, stackable FROM item_template WHERE stackable > 1;
sql.note: INSERT IGNORE so a second install never overwrites the ORIGINAL values with this mod's own

sql.statement: UPDATE item_template SET stackable = {stack_size} WHERE stackable > 1;
UPDATE item_template t JOIN yulon_stackable_backup b ON b.entry = t.entry SET t.stackable = b.stackable;

prompts.question: Max stack size for stackable items

notes: There is no repo to clone: on CMaNGOS a SQL mod is inline SQL against `mangos`, this
game's world schema (`db: world` -> `CatalogEntry.schema_map()`), because the mods
published for this are all AzerothCore-flavoured and would not apply.
The column is this fork's own: `item_template`.`stackable` is `smallint(5) unsigned` in
It carries its own undo. `item_template` is loaded from vanilla-db, so the values it
overwrites are not recoverable from anywhere else once changed - the backup table is
the only thing that makes Remove mean anything. Do not drop it by hand.
`WHERE stackable > 1` leaves non-stackable items alone; an item whose stack is already
larger than the chosen size is lowered to it, which is why the backup is taken first.
Verify with: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM item_template WHERE stackable = <size>;
